title: Fifteen Years of the Premier League: What Sustained Success Looks Like
summary: Fifteen seasons of Premier League data connect institutional persistence with fair comparison, attack–defence efficiency and the limits of simple discipline models.
key_takeaway: Dominance is balanced performance sustained over time: the clubs that stay on top score heavily, control their defensive downside and keep rebuilding that balance through changing squads and managers. It resists the tidy explanations built on one peripheral statistic, including a discipline formula that this analysis deliberately tested and found no real signal for. Sustained success is a system, not a signature stat.

inline_figures.caption: League-position points across fifteen seasons show a steep elite tier and a long tail of shorter or less successful top-flight records.
